{{short description|Triangle derived from a given triangle and a coplanar point}}

In [[Euclidean geometry]], a '''circumcevian triangle''' is a special [[triangle]] associated with a reference triangle and a point in the plane of the triangle. It is also associated with the [[circumcircle]] of the reference triangle.

==Definition==
[[File:CircumCevianTriangle.png|thumb|
{{legend-line|solid blue|Reference triangle {{math|△''ABC''}}}}
{{legend|red|Point {{mvar|P}}}}
{{legend-line|solid #222222|Circumcircle of {{math|△''ABC''}}; lines between the vertices of {{math|△''ABC''}} and {{mvar|P}}}}
{{legend-line|solid brown|Circumcevian triangle {{math|△''A'B'C'''}} of {{mvar|P}}}}
]]

Let {{mvar|P}} be a point in the plane of the reference triangle {{math|△''ABC''}}. Let the lines {{mvar|AP, BP, CP}} intersect the [[circumcircle]] of {{math|△''ABC''}} at {{mvar|A', B', C'}}. The triangle {{math|△''A'B'C'''}} is called the '''circumcevian triangle''' of {{mvar|P}} with reference to {{math|△''ABC''}}.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Kimberling, C |title=Triangle Centers and Central Triangles |journal=Congress Numerantium |date=1998 |volume=129 |page=201}}</ref>

==Coordinates==
Let {{mvar|a,b,c}} be the side lengths of triangle {{math|△''ABC''}} and let the [[trilinear coordinates]] of {{mvar|P}} be {{math|''&alpha;'' : ''&beta;'' : ''&gamma;''}}. Then the trilinear coordinates of the vertices of the circumcevian triangle of {{mvar|P}} are as follows:<ref name="Wolfram">{{cite web |last1=Weisstein, Eric W. |title="Circumcevian Triangle" |url=https://mathworld.wolfram.com/CircumcevianTriangle.html |website=From MathWorld--A Wolfram Web Resource. |publisher=MathWorld |access-date=24 December 2021}}</ref>
<math display=block>\begin{array}{rccccc}
  A' =& -a\beta\gamma &:& (b\gamma+c\beta)\beta &:& (b\gamma+c\beta)\gamma \\
  B' =& (c\alpha +a\gamma)\alpha &:& - b\gamma\alpha &:& (c\alpha +a\gamma) \gamma \\
  C' =& (a\beta +b\alpha)\alpha &:& (a\beta +b\alpha)\beta &:& - c\alpha\beta
\end{array}</math>

==Some properties==
*Every triangle inscribed in the circumcircle of the reference triangle ABC is congruent to exactly one circumcevian triangle.<ref name="Wolfram"/>
*The circumcevian triangle of P is similar to the [[pedal triangle]] of P.<ref name="Wolfram"/>
*The [[McCay cubic]] is the locus of point P such that the circumcevian triangle of P and ABC are [[Orthologic triangles|orthologic]].<ref name="K003">{{cite web |last1=Bernard Gilbert |title=K003 McCay Cubic |url=https://bernard-gibert.pagesperso-orange.fr/Exemples/k003.html |website=Catalogue of Triangle Cubics |publisher=Bernard Gilbert |access-date=24 December 2021}}</ref>
